clue.text: Colonel retreating to American position

indicators.note: a retreating army goes back the way it came, so this word is read from right to left

blocks.note: Col is the standard abbreviation for colonel
US stands for the United States, so American

explanation.surface: An army officer withdraws to a post held by US forces.
explanation.walkthrough: LOC (COL backwards) then US gives LOCUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A locus is a place or site, formally a point's location, so a synonym for position.

clue.text: Glowing gently, get up without energy following sexual passion

indicators.note: without here means lacking, so the letter for energy is dropped

blocks.note: lust is strong sexual desire
to rouse is to get someone up
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A sensual afterglow and no energy to get out of bed after passion.
explanation.walkthrough: E is the physics symbol for energy, the letter dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustrous means having a soft sheen, shining with reflected light.

clue.text: Path once re-routed for construction in Whitehall

indicators.note: a re-routed journey takes a different course, so these letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A street once diverted to make way for building works in London's government district.
explanation.walkthrough: Whitehall is the London street of government offices, home to Britain's national war memorial.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cenotaph is the war memorial standing in Whitehall, a built monument there.

clue.text: Remove spent film after getting shot — this helps one get better still

definitions.text: this helps one get better still

indicators.note: something shot to pieces is wrecked and scattered, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: fifteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Photographic advice: take out the used film after shooting, to get a better still picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like a photograph; it means 'even more'. 'Shot' means wrecked, not photographed.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-improvement is the work of making oneself better through one's own efforts.

clue.text: ONMLKJIH

blocks.note: surface reading: a stretch of the alphabet written out of order, from O down to H
setter's reading: the letters H to O, written backwards; H to O reads like H2O, the chemical formula of a familiar liquid

explanation.surface: A puzzling string of letters, the alphabet run in reverse from O to H.
explanation.walkthrough: H to O stands for H2O, so this is H-to-O written backwards: BACK plus WATER.
explanation.definitionFit: A backwater is a stretch of still water off a river's main stream, the literal sense the letter picture builds.

clue.text: Tub on the Kennet and Avon canal

definitions.text: on the Kennet and Avon canal

blocks.note: first meaning: a vessel to wash in

blocks.clueFragment: on the Kennet and Avon canal
blocks.note: second meaning: the English spa city through which this canal runs

explanation.walkthrough: The Kennet and Avon is an English canal linking Reading with the Somerset spa city famed for Roman baths.
explanation.definitionFit: A bath is a tub for washing, and also the name of the Somerset city on that canal.

clue.text: A scale in C?

blocks.note: surface reading: a musical scale in the key of C
setter's reading: C is the symbol for degrees on a temperature scale

explanation.surface: A musician practising a scale in the key of C.
explanation.walkthrough: C is not the musical key but the temperature unit.
explanation.definitionFit: This temperature scale, now called Celsius, is abbreviated C, with water freezing at 0 and boiling at 100.

clue.text: Fit and full of purpose, but on the way to hell?

blocks.note: first meaning: read in parts, healthy and full of aims
second meaning: the proverb says the road to hell is paved with good aims

explanation.walkthrough: The first half splits the answer into its parts: fit, and full of purpose. The question mark flags the proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: Meaning well but not necessarily doing good, which the proverb says leads to hell.

clue.text: Stand, taking journey leaving centre of Oxford

indicators.note: leaving out the centre of a word means its middle letters are dropped

blocks.note: a trip is a journey
taken as written before losing its middle

explanation.surface: Taking a stand on a trip out of central Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first and last letters of the city survive.
explanation.definitionFit: A tripod is a three-legged stand, as for a camera.

clue.text: Thomas of Erceldoune, or similar sound writer

blocks.note: first meaning: the 13th-century Scottish poet known as Thomas the ___
second meaning: someone who writes words ending in matching sounds

explanation.walkthrough: Thomas of Erceldoune was a medieval Scottish poet and seer, remembered by his nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhymer is a writer of verse with matching end sounds, and Thomas's traditional nickname.

clue.text: One in a suit needing vest on

blocks.note: a singlet is a sleeveless vest
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wearing a suit still needs a vest underneath it.
explanation.walkthrough: The suit is a suit of cards, not clothes; in Britain a vest is an undershirt, which is what a singlet is.
explanation.definitionFit: In card games a singleton is a hand's only card in a particular suit.

clue.text: All but the clergy exorcise without it

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one word sits around the other

blocks.note: to lay a ghost is to exorcise it
taken as written

explanation.surface: Everyone except the priests performs exorcisms, without help from it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking' but is the old word for outside. To lay a ghost is to exorcise it.
explanation.definitionFit: The laity are the ordinary members of a church, everyone who is not ordained.

clue.text: Keep control when fighters enter

indicators.note: to enter something is to go inside it, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: to rein in is to control
the TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: Holding on to command of a castle while soldiers storm in.
explanation.walkthrough: TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: To retain something is to continue possessing it, a direct synonym for keep as a verb.

clue.text: What's used in breast implants since oil is unstable

indicators.note: something unstable will not hold its shape, so these letters fall into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A reason for using a certain gel in cosmetic surgery: oil is unstable.
explanation.definitionFit: Silicone gel is the familiar filling of cosmetic breast implants.

clue.text: Sniffs fuel, getting high — the down has this characteristic

indicators.note: someone getting high is in an altered state, so these letters are altered in order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A glue-sniffer getting high, with the comedown that follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The down' looks like a crash after a high, or a crossword direction; it is soft feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: Down is the soft fine feathering of birds, whose quality is a soft, airy lightness.

clue.text: The sort of public reaction one is out to get

definitions.text: The sort of public reaction one is out to get

blocks.clueFragment: The sort of public reaction one is out to get
blocks.note: surface reading: a response from the public that someone is deliberately seeking
setter's reading: out means out of favour, so this is the reaction a person gets when people stop liking them

explanation.surface: A provocateur seeking a particular response from the public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out to get' suggests intent; read instead 'one is out' (out of favour), and what one gets.
explanation.definitionFit: Unpopularity is the state of being disliked by the public, what someone fallen from favour receives.

clue.text: Detective Inspector's imaginative plan for some police?

blocks.note: DI is the abbreviation for detective inspector
a vision is an imaginative plan for the future

explanation.surface: A police officer's bold strategy for part of the force.
explanation.definitionFit: A division is an administrative section of a police force, so some police; the question mark flags the loose phrasing.

clue.text: Like wild weather? See sky's colour across the way, over the railway

indicators.note: lying across something spans it, so one piece stretches around the other

blocks.note: surface padding, pointing the eye at the sky
the sky's colour is blue
St is the abbreviation for street
Ry is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: Watching the sky's colour across the road and above the railway line as storms brew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is only a pointer in the surface. In a down clue, 'over' puts the first part above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Blustery describes gusty, stormy weather with strong winds.

clue.text: Graham Greene's agent not expecting publication

blocks.note: first meaning: Greene wrote the 1939 thriller The ___ Agent
second meaning: private, meant to be kept secret

explanation.surface: A novelist's literary agent who isn't anticipating a book coming out.
explanation.walkthrough: The agent is a spy from a Greene title, not a literary agent.
explanation.definitionFit: Confidential material is private and not intended to be made public; the word also completes the Greene novel title.

clue.text: Part of neck — namely, over frilly collar

blocks.note: sc, for Latin scilicet, means namely
a ruff is a frilled Elizabethan collar

explanation.surface: Pointing out an area of neck beneath a frilled collar.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'over' puts SC above RUFF.
explanation.definitionFit: The scruff is the back of the neck, as in grabbing someone by the scruff.

clue.text: Feel curious and flushed before present turns up

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up flips the letters so they read from bottom to top

blocks.note: flushed in the face is red
the present time is now

explanation.surface: Curious and red-faced as a gift arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole of RED then NOW turns over, not just the present.
explanation.definitionFit: To wonder is to be curious and want to know something.

clue.text: Bad-tempered priest suppressing cry of derision

indicators.note: to suppress something is to hold it down inside, so one piece is held within the other

blocks.note: a cleric is a priest
ho is an exclamation of scorn or derision

explanation.surface: A grumpy vicar holding back a mocking jeer.
explanation.definitionFit: Choleric describes an irritable, quick-to-anger temperament, from the old humour of yellow bile.

clue.text: Courses immigrants value in citizenship studies start with this?

definitions.text: Courses immigrants value in citizenship studies start with this?

indicators.note: the start of each word is what is wanted, so only opening letters are kept

blocks.clueFragment: Courses immigrants value in citizenship studies
blocks.note: the first letters of these six words

explanation.surface: Asks whether citizenship classes for new arrivals begin with this subject.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Civics is the study of citizens' rights and duties and how government works, the core of citizenship classes.

clue.text: Recess at the heart of abandoned church?

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle, so only the central letters are kept

blocks.note: abandoned, as a faith is, is LAPSED; its middle four letters
surface padding that fits the scene of a disused building

explanation.surface: Asks whether there is a recess at the centre of a disused church.
explanation.walkthrough: Abandoned stands for LAPSED, which loses its outer letters; the church only supplies the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is a vaulted recess at the end of a church, so a recess.

clue.text: Unwarranted German and European Union backing

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the letters it follows are read the other way round

blocks.note: und is German for 'and'
the usual abbreviation

explanation.surface: Germany and the EU giving support that wasn't justified.
explanation.definitionFit: Undue means excessive or not justified, a synonym of unwarranted.

clue.text: A partner that was thoughtful and dear

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
pensive means deep in thought

explanation.surface: Remembering a former lover who was considerate and much loved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dear' looks like a word of affection; it means costly.
explanation.definitionFit: Dear in the sense of high-priced, so a synonym for costly.

clue.text: Sampler played loudly either side of rest days regularly taken

indicators.note: taking things at regular intervals means every second letter is kept
one thing on either side of another wraps around it, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: forte is the musical term for loud
the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: Someone playing a musical sampler loudly around their rest days.
explanation.walkthrough: A sampler here is a taster, not a music device or embroidery.
explanation.definitionFit: A foretaste is a small early experience of something to come, like a sample.

clue.text: Attractively small daughter, very dark

blocks.note: d is the abbreviation for daughter
inky means black as ink

explanation.surface: Describing a petite daughter with very dark colouring.
explanation.walkthrough: Dinky is British for pleasingly small and neat.
explanation.definitionFit: Dinky is a British informal word for small and neat in a cute way.
